name: nostra-chat
description: Nostra.chat is a 100% client-side Progressive Web App for decentralized messaging, forked from Telegram Web K. It replaces the Telegram backend with peer-to-peer encrypted chat over Nostr relays and integrates Tor via WASM for network-level privacy. No servers, no accounts, no install — just cryptographic keys and a browser.

paragraphs: Privacy-first decentralized messaging with end-to-end encryption and anonymous relay-based delivery.

Nostra.chat is a 100% client-side Progressive Web App for decentralized messaging, forked from Telegram Web K. It replaces the Telegram backend with peer-to-peer encrypted chat over Nostr relays and integrates Tor via WASM for network-level privacy.
No central application server. No accounts. No native install. Just cryptographic keys, independent relays, optional supporting services, and a browser.
features: 1:1 encrypted text messaging with real-time delivery over Nostr relays
Group chats up to 12 members using NIP-17 multi-recipient gift-wrap — relay operators cannot determine group membership
Encrypted photo and file sharing via Blossom blob storage (AES-256-GCM); broader video/voice interoperability remains under verification
Message deletion (local and remote via NIP-09 kind 5)
Replies, edits, and emoji reactions over the Nostra transport

whatItDoes.text: Privacy-first decentralized messaging with end-to-end encryption and anonymous relay-based delivery.

requirements.text: SimpleX uses SMP relay servers; anyone can self-host, but most users rely on the project-operated defaults.
SimpleX has no account system — each installation is a separate identity.
The push relay is open source (nostr-webpush-relay) and operates over NIP-98-authenticated registration; users can swap the endpoint to a self-hosted instance at any time.

Nostra.chat's positioning is different: fully decentralized over Nostr relays, with user-owned keys, no account to create, censorship-resistant mirror distribution including IPFS, and zero installation — all in the browser.
